prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (2001)

Constitution and governance
- Seek a referendum on Scottish independence and expanded powers for the Scottish Parliament; a majority of the manifesto’s Westminster MPs would trigger a referendum.
- Written constitution with defined rights and responsibilities; automatic citizenship for residents, those born in Scotland, and those with a Scottish-born parent (others may apply).
- Retain the monarch as head of state subject to referendum consent.
- Proportional representation at all government levels.
- Reduce and reform quangos; increase parliamentary oversight.
- Create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations using surplus oil revenues, and a Scottish Trust for Public Investment (STPI) to finance infrastructure more cheaply than PFI/PPP.

Education and children
- Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants as resources allow; support Cubie recommendations on benefits.
- Lower voting age to 16; establish a Children’s Commissioner; implement UNCRC.
- Establish an Education Convention; temporary moratorium on further structural change.
- Reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18 (prioritising deprived areas); end publication of league tables; refurbish schools via STPI.
- Expand Gaelic-medium education; support inclusive education, anti-racism, and recognition of Catholic school needs.

Economy, jobs, and tourism
- Infrastructure investment (road, rail, sea, air), universal broadband, skills/reskilling, refocused enterprise agencies.
- Devolve and redesign employment programmes to target job black spots.
- Raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages, with mitigations for small firms via tax reform.
- Charter of Trade Union Rights; support EU employee involvement laws.
- Reorient tourism bodies toward marketing; improve access and gateway air links.

Environment, water, and energy
- State of the Nation Environmental Audit and National Environment Plan; contribute to climate goals.
- 12% of total energy and 25% of electricity from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear; decommission at end of life.
- Strengthen SEPA oversight (including military sites).
- Review water charges, halt privatisation by stealth, protect low-income users, democratise water governance.

Health and social care
- Create a National Health Care Commission; end postcode treatment with binding Health Technology Board decisions.
- Free fruit in primary schools; nutritional standards for school meals.
- Free dental check-ups; review/freeze prescription charges.
- Invest in equipment; £4m Clean Hospitals Fund; recruit at least 1,500 nurses; halve inpatient waiting times.
- Free personal care for older people.

Justice and policing
- £25m for 1,000 additional police officers.
- Youth justice and parental responsibility measures, including possible compensation orders.
- Implement lifelong restriction orders for high-risk sexual/violent offenders; expand supervised release; strengthen sex offender registration.
- Sentencing Advisory Panel; faster lower-court cases; retain more fine revenues in Scotland.

Europe, defence, and international
- Support EU membership with stronger subsidiarity and retained vetoes on resources, tax, and constitutional issues; possible euro entry by referendum when conditions allow.
- Remove Trident from Scotland; oppose US missile defence; phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining cooperation; create a professional Scottish Defence Force.
- Consolidate overseas trade, investment, and tourism representation; untie aid, target UN benchmarks, reform HIPC, establish “Aid from Scotland.”

Housing, welfare, and equality
- Seek UK assumption of historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via STPI; oppose wholesale stock transfer.
- Core, multi‑year funding for voluntary sector; end competitive “challenge” schemes; exempt from water charges.
- National anti-poverty strategy and “poverty proofing.”
- Extend Disability Discrimination Act; introduce disability equality indicator; streamline disability benefits and support carers.
- Review Working Families Tax Credit taper effects; improve benefit take-up; consider winter fuel aid for severely disabled under 60.

Taxation and local government
- No overall tax burden increase without mandate; comprehensive tax review for fairness and simplicity.
- Immediate 10p/gal fuel duty cut funded by a new 5p income tax band over £100k.
- Review local government finance, including local income tax; support PR/STV for councils.

Rural, agriculture, fisheries, land
- Fuel duty cut; small business rates relief; ICT and transport improvements; protect rural services; crisis contingency funds.
- Post–foot-and-mouth agricultural review; fair EU implementation; support diversification, organics, LFAs reform.
- Compensated tie-ups, conservation measures, and zonal management in fisheries; support processing and aquaculture; salmon farming inquiry.
- Expand community rights over land and freshwater fisheries.

Pensions
- Restore earnings link for the basic state pension using NI surplus; address MIG distortions; spread winter fuel payments weekly.

Transport
- Secure fair UK investment share; create Regional Transport Authorities; single transport safety authority; ATC in public sector.
- Public stake in Railtrack for accountability; reopen key lines and airport links; targeted electrification; national concessionary travel scheme.
- Road maintenance plus limited new capacity (e.g., M74 extension, Aberdeen bypass, A9 upgrades); reduce ferry fares and pilot Road Equivalent Tariff; more direct flights; abolish Skye Bridge tolls and explore public trust ownership.

Broadcasting, culture, languages, sport
- Devolve broadcasting oversight; accelerate digital transition; increase BBC Scotland autonomy; pursue a national “Scottish Six.”
- Reform arts funding; establish a national theatre and a “Scottish Academy”; increase support for traditional arts; consider a Scottish Lottery.
- Strengthen Gaelic and Scots language status, education, and media use.
- Focus sports funding on community activity; develop football academies; bid for major tournaments.
